commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 certify (PR #1300): diff changes the Brazil gate in every generated composition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` and re-grounds the steel parameter proof from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; report says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage".
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The Brazil IEEPA exception was conditioned on the witness's exemplar line identity `entry_is_line_b` rather than Section 232 aluminum membership, so the 40% Brazil surcharge was added to aluminum entries the cited 9903.01.77 exception exempts.

triage.verifier_justification: I tried three refutations and all fail. The diff is not provenance-only: alongside the steel-parameter re-grounding (9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02, where the formula stays '0.50', i.e. genuinely mechanical), two formula lines change the IEEPA gate condition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, which is encoded meaning. It is also not "new scope the module never claimed": the pre-fix `ieepa_component_rate` rule carries its own proof atom `kind: exception` citing "The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02.", and the pre-fix module summary already asserts that "section-232 aluminum ... identifiers are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation" — so the gate keyed on the five-line witness's exemplar identity `entry_is_line_b` contradicted both the cited source and the module's own declared surface. The resolver confirms 9903.01.77 is the Brazil IEEPA "+ 40%" heading whose exceptions are defined by product headings (9903.01.78–.83, .90), never by a line identity, so the old condition had no basis in the cited text and the fix re-grounds it — untraceable_branch, not polarity (the negation is preserved) and not wrong_entity_or_scope (entity, geography and rate are unchanged).

inferred from verified sibling module index 0 (same kind and rule path in this chunk). Mixed commit: the second half of the diff (ch01_s232_steel_heading_rate / section_232_steel_component_rate proof atoms re-cited from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02, two atoms collapsed to one) is citation-path/excerpt-only with formula '0.50' unchanged, i.e. mechanical provenance; the report's own words are "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage: Rev. 15 contains no operative 9903.81.x row and consolidates the charge at 9903.82.02." Only the two IEEPA gate lines carry the fidelity finding, so if the corpus keys the case on rule_names it should key on rules[ieepa_component_rate] / [ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions], not on the steel rules.

Duplicate-coverage risk for the reviewer: the generator already contained the substitution pair `"ieepa_component_rate": (("not entry_is_line_b", "not entry_is_section_232_aluminum"),)` at the PARENT commit a9562cfd ("b1.6: generalize generated component surfaces"); only the emitted YAML lagged, and this commit regenerates. `git -C rulespec-us show a9562cfd -- tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py` shows it. If a9562cfd (or 2a6bdb01d) is also screened into the corpus, the same underlying defect may appear twice — this commit is the emission, that one is the intent.

Not intra-PR scaffolding: the generated file was first added in aa44a141b ("Generated tariff-schedule compositions, batch 1 of the B1.3 series"), which is an ancestor of origin/main, so the exemplar-flag gate shipped at schedule scale before PR #1300.

Two caveats on the first reader's stated consequence, neither changing the verdict: (1) the "40% added to aluminum entries" incidence claim depends on `entry_is_line_b` evaluating FALSE for real aluminum lines at schedule scale — the natural reading of a caller-supplied exemplar flag, but I did not execute the module to confirm; (2) the affected version window is narrow — the branch runs `from: '2026-02-15'` and is superseded at `from: '2026-02-20'` by `terminated_ieepa_additional_ad_valorem_duty_rate`, so the mis-grounded gate is live for roughly five days of encoded time. Also note the new gate is a close but not exact match to the source: `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` covers the module's whole §232 aluminum membership (9903.85.08 content-basis, 9903.85.67 Russia, etc.) while the cited carve-out names products "provided for in heading 9903.85.02" — an approximation in the right direction, not a reason to reject.

Corpus-vintage note: resolving us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219 through the pinned release returns a Rev. 3 note page (a subheading list), not the aluminum carve-out sentence — page numbering differs from the Rev. 15 vintage the module is grounded on, so the excerpt is not independently verifiable through the pinned resolver. 9903.01.77 itself resolves and confirms Brazil +40% with heading-defined exceptions.
